quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: What do rumble strips do?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They use vibration and sound to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They use vibration and sound to warn drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibrations. They warn tired or inattentive drivers when they drift off the road or approach a stop sign or traffic light.

questions.question: If an accident causes $1,000 or more in property damage, you do not have to report it.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must report any accident that causes $1,000 or more in property damage to police or the local sheriff. You must also report any accident that causes injuries. Failing to report an accident can result in criminal charges and license suspension.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which of these is dangerous in a work zone?

options.text: Driving too close behind another vehicle.
Not watching for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Pay attention to workers and equipment around you.

questions.question: Why is night driving harder than daytime driving?

options.text: Cars overheat more at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
Rain is more likely at night.
You are more likely to meet motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Always use your headlights. Drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: When must you use your low beam headlights?

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water and cause glare, making it harder to see. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A yellow traffic light means the light will soon turn red. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, what should you do?

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, drive through as quickly as possible to clear it.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your side mirror, rearview mirror, and blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic.
Let freeway traffic go first.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed up on the on-ramp to match freeway traffic speed and let traffic already on the freeway go first. Use your mirrors and check blind spots to find a safe space to merge.

questions.question: Is night driving safer or more dangerous than daytime driving?

options.text: Safer.
About the same.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than daytime driving. It is harder to see in darkness. Bright lights from other cars can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic is coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads to increase your speed?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride up on water and cause you to lose control. This is called hydroplaning. To avoid this, slow down when driving on wet roads.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When conditions are not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any condition is not ideal. You can be ticketed for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are within the speed limit.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a stopped school bus with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk your horn before passing on the left.
Continue driving when you think most children have exited.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm extended. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on the radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest.
Move your eyes side to side as you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest.
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly. Rest and stretch, even if you do not feel tired.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and use light braking.
Brake firmly and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, slow down gradually by taking your foot off the accelerator. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed down.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that affects your driving ability?

options.text: Never.
Yes, if you do not feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while taking any substance that impairs your driving. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve.
On a road with a solid line next to your lane.
On a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross and change lanes. A solid line means you cannot. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Is it safe to stop on railroad tracks for a short time while moving with traffic?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never stop, stand, or park on railroad tracks. Only cross railroad tracks if your entire vehicle can fit on the other side.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
The lane must turn right.
Turn right only on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns of a sharp right turn ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
A roundabout is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and carpools only.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with more than one lane in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, how far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would behind a car.
Farther than you would behind a car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than you would behind a car.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind a large truck than you would behind a car. Large trucks have bigger blind spots.

questions.question: What should you do when a large vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Speed up.
Change lanes.
Keep your speed the same or slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your speed the same or slow down.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when a large vehicle is passing you. Keep your speed the same or slow down slightly to let the large vehicle pass safely.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are intersections ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign alerts drivers that the number of lanes will decrease ahead. Traffic should merge left.

questions.question: Is the posted speed limit the fastest you can legally drive?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed under normal conditions. You must drive slower when conditions require it, such as on wet roads or when visibility is poor.

questions.question: When can you drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. Once the gate is raised, do not cross the tracks until you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from the rear, press yourself against the back of your seat and press your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Keep a firm grip on the steering wheel and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, regardless of other signals. You must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single broken white centerline mean?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross it to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross it to change lanes.
questions.explanation: A broken white centerline means lanes are traveling in the same direction. It is legal to pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.
Do not turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an approaching vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road you cannot see without moving your head.

options.text: You cannot see without moving your head.
Directly behind your vehicle.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without moving your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: To make a right turn properly, you should:

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb, but move over toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, use your signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and stay in the right lane, as close to the right curb as possible.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic from another road may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: A driver entering a highway from an entrance or acceleration ramp should:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Has the right-of-way.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering a highway, you must yield to drivers already on it. Merge safely when there is space.

questions.question: If traffic lights at an intersection are not working due to a power outage, you should:

options.text: Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.
Use hand signals to indicate your intentions to other drivers.
Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.
Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers, then proceed with caution when it is your turn.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors, as they cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be ready to stop?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be cautious, and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, you should:

options.text: Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.
Stop on the first railroad track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one of the tracks is free.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait to proceed until you have a clear view of all tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not cross until you can see clearly down all tracks. A second train may be coming even after one passes.

questions.question: Your car may hydroplane on wet roads at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Most tires can handle standing water up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires cannot push water away fast enough and may lose contact with the road.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
No right turns permitted.
Right turns permitted on a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns permitted.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits right turns. It is illegal to turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision at an intersection. No one is hurt and there is little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for current conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers staying four seconds behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Your tire suddenly goes flat while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake hard. Let the vehicle slow on its own. Use brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when safe.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs warn you that you are near a school. When you see these signs, stay alert and be prepared to stop.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when it first starts to rain. On a slippery road, you should:

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tire grip by driving uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower on wet roads than on dry roads. Avoid fast turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: Which of the following slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a collision.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a collision.
questions.explanation: Looking at collisions or accidents (rubbernecking) slows traffic and causes congestion. Avoid this behavior.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, the safest thing to do is:

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive slower than other traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with traffic flow while staying within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and cause glare, making it harder to see. Fog lights can also be used with low beams.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed and go through the water.
Avoid the puddle if possible.
Shift into neutral as you drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the puddle if possible.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. The safest surface to drive on is dry and solid.

questions.question: You find a vehicle defect that may affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have the money.
Drive at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe driving as soon as possible. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: When can you go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check that no traffic is coming
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any intersection with a stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights:

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog. High beams will bounce off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, when should you signal?

options.text: Just before changing lanes
At any time
After changing lanes
Early enough so other drivers know your plans

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know your plans
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know what you plan to do.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red light without stopping. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green
Go through the intersection without stopping
Come to a complete stop before proceeding

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions instead of traffic signals or signs. The officer is directing traffic and has authority over the signals.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights in fog, not high beams. High beams bounce back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When a school bus stops ahead to load or unload children, what must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop until all children leave the bus
Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the arm is pulled back before you go. Even then, make sure no children are crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Multiple turns
Lane shifting
Do not block intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to allow merging traffic to enter safely.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers
Get closer to the car in front
Pass carefully and do not stare at the construction

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not stare at the construction
questions.explanation: Do not stare at construction or unusual things on the road. This slows traffic and causes congestion. Keep your eyes on the road and drive through the zone carefully.

questions.question: When can a driver pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?

options.text: When the shoulder is paved
When the car in front is waiting to turn left
When the car in front is driving under the speed limit
Never

questions.correctAnswerText: Never
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. Other drivers will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder without looking, hitting your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Divided highway
Railroad warning
No passing zone

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a divided highway is starting ahead.
